Fundamental

fun-duh-MEN-tuhl · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Fundamental is basic, important, and necessary; forming the base of something.

Passing the ball is a fundamental skill every soccer player learns first.

Worked Example

Trust is fundamental to a good friendship - without it, the friendship falls apart.

The sentence says the friendship falls apart without trust. That shows trust sits at the very base of friendship - a fundamental part.

How Fundamental Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

essential

essential: absolutely needed

basic

basic: at the base or start of something

Antonyms

unimportant

unimportant: not mattering much

optional

optional: something you can skip

How Strong Is It? — Helpful → fundamental → Essential

Helpful vs. fundamental

Helpful vs. fundamental: Helpful is a lighter word: a pencil grip is helpful for writing, but you could still write without it.

Essential vs. fundamental

Essential vs. fundamental: Essential is even stronger: water is essential for every living thing - nothing can live without it.

Put it together

Put it together: Fundament means a base, so something fundamental is part of the base that everything else is built on.

Word Choice

Fundamental is a slightly serious word - great for skills, rules, or ideas that everything else depends on. Its close cousin vital means needed for life or success.
